newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Retevision rejects Unisource delay request.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Retevision rejects Unisource delay request.

text.p: Retevision, which will soon become Spain's second basic telephone operator, rejected consortium Unisource's request for more time to submit its statement of interest in purchasing 60 percent of the group.

"The Retevision sale committee will propose to the board that Unisource's request to delay the deadline for presenting its candidacy be denied," a Retevision spokesman told Reuters on Friday, confirming a report in Expansion newspaper.

This means Unisource will not be allowed to present an independent bid for the 60 percent stake in Retevision that the state is selling, although it will be allowed to join its effort with the other three groups of bidders.
She added that the formal announcement of the decision will be made after Retevision board's meeting on Wednesday, April 30.

AT&T-led Unisource is a consortium of telecoms flagships from the Netherlands, Switzerland and Sweden. It presented on Monday this week a formal declaration to participate in the auction, asking for a delay.

Retevision said three international consortia had requested to join the bid: Mannesmann and AT&T ; a group including Deutsche Telekom, France Telecom, Sprint Corp and BCH ; and a group including Stet International, Endesa, Union Fenosa and Basque group Euskatel.
Since these groups have time to change their composition until May 12, Unisource could now join an alliance with AT&T and Mannesman.
But some analysts say a deal would also be possible between Unisource and the other group, led by Italy's Stet.
This would be likely if Stet buys the stake in Unisource that Spain's Telefonica may sell.
Industry sources said that Spain's Development Ministry may prefer a bid from an alliance between the BCH and Endesa groups, but talks between the two are still at an early stage.
